Harlequins Edge Exeter Chiefs in Nine-Try Premiership Thriller at Sandy Park

01 Nov 2026, 10:43 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Harlequins Claim Consecutive League Wins

Harlequins secured back-to-back Premiership victories for the first time this season following a hard-fought win against Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park. The high-scoring encounter featured nine tries in total, culminating in a tense finish that ultimately favored the visitors.

According to match reports, Harlequins started strongly under clear conditions in Devon, establishing an early lead before the hosts mounted a sustained comeback.

Match Breakdown and Scoring

  • Early Visitors' Advantage: Cadan Murley opened the scoring for Harlequins, finishing off a move initiated by George Furbank and Marcus Smith. Nick David soon extended the lead to put the visitors firmly ahead in the opening exchanges.
  • Exeter Fightback: The Chiefs responded through a close-range try by lock Harry Wilson. Despite a yellow card shown to Harlequins' Bryn Bradley, Exeter capitalized on the numerical advantage just before half-time when Nika Abuladze crossed the line to level the score.
  • Lead Changes: Will Butt put the hosts ahead shortly after the break following a missed tackle in midfield. However, Harlequins reclaimed momentum through a quick-fire brace from number eight Lucas Schmid, who scored two close-range tries.
  • Tense Conclusion: Late scores from Jack Kenningham for Harlequins and Olly Woodburn for Exeter narrowed the gap to three points. With the clock in the red, Exeter lost possession at a crucial lineout, allowing Harlequins to kick the ball into touch and seal the victory.

Practical Implications and Verification

With this result, Harlequins continue their winning run in the league, while Exeter Chiefs reflect on missed opportunities despite a competitive display featuring tries from Wilson, Abuladze, Butt, and Woodburn alongside four conversions by Henry Slade. Harlequins' scoring efforts included tries from Murley, David, Schmid (2), and Kenningham, with three conversions added by Marcus Smith.
